newsitem.title: UK: Russian straight run fuel thinned, but still around.
newsitem.headline: Russian straight run fuel thinned, but still around.

text.p: Active trade in Russian straight run fuel on Wednesday thinned supplies significantly, but material still remains available.
Traders said at least two E-4 and three M-100 cargoes found homes but a further four first half December cargoes remain.
Traders who have been talking about Russian material drying up have had to re-adjust.

"I've been saying it would dry up for ages and sooner or later it will," said one trader. Interest continues as to when the Russians will levy the main winter mazut export tariff, but there has been no firm confirmation from Moscow.

In the cracked market high sulphur barges continued to show a slight contango with prompt material trading as low as $117.50 early on Thursday morning. Prices and activity picked up with material for prompt and December barrels pegged around $119-121 fob ARA. Bunker demand was moderate around 10-15,000 tonnes.

High sulphur cracked cargoes were steady at $120 cif NWE with very little material on offer. End-user demand was viewed by some dealers as muted, but enough to give support to a tightish market. Low sulphur held steady close to $132 fob NWE, gaining suppport from strong U.S. natural gas prices.
